messages:
Customer Rep (Acme): Hey — multiple customers on Acme App reporting SSE generation streams truncating mid-event. They see partial chunks and then client reconnect loops. Attaching a small pcap and a curl repro. Example repro: 

curl -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-large' --no-buffer

Behavior: first ~200-1200 tokens stream fine, then stream stops mid-chunk (no final event), client attempts reconnect, sometimes gets 401 or 402 for that reconnect, sometimes gets immediate EOF. Ticket: ACME-789. Anyone seen billing/auth mid-stream causing this?

Alyssa (support): Thanks — can you paste a sample of the raw client output (with partial chunk) and the timestamp/trace id from the original request? Also confirm whether the token is short-lived (mobile SDK) or static.

Customer Rep (Acme): Pasted below. Trace: trc-9a7b2d7c. Client raw: 

data: {"id":"abc123", "choices": ["The quick brown"

  (stream stops here)

} 

And attached pcap: https://internal-artifacts/acme/pcaps/ACME-789.pcapng

Matt (eng-runtime): Looking. Quick note: SSE connections are long-lived and we expect client reconnects to use resume (stream resume token). If reconnect auth fails we will drop finalization and you see partial output.

Matt (eng-runtime): I pulled edge logs for trc-9a7b2d7c: edge accepted connection, proxied to runtime, runtime returned a 200 then emitted a close. Edge log snippet: 

```
[2026-03-10T19:12:23Z] trace=trc-9a7b2d7c conn_id=9876 method=POST path=/v1/streams status=200 stream_start=0 stream_end=null backend=runtime-12
[2026-03-10T19:12:52Z] trace=trc-9a7b2d7c conn_id=9876 backend_conn=runtime-12 event=backend_reset reason=token_revoked
[2026-03-10T19:12:52Z] trace=trc-9a7b2d7c conn_id=9876 event=edge_close code=1011
```

Matt (eng-runtime): 'token_revoked' is our internal tag when the billing/auth service indicates account in a bad state mid-stream (e.g., billing limit hit, account suspended, or token rotation mismatch). Not common, but plausible here.

Jordan (sre): I pulled firewall/transport side from the pcap. Observations: TLS session closes with FIN from server side at 19:12:52, then client reconnects and gets TLS handshake + HTTP/1.1 402 Payment Required from edge. Packet-level: we see no RSTs from runtime; graceful close. Means server intentionally closed stream.

Jordan (sre): pcap excerpt: 

- server TLS close_notify at packet 24012 (19:12:52)
- client SYN at 19:12:53 for reconnect; server responds 200-> then 402 on reconnect request

Alyssa (support): So summary so far: stream closed gracefully because backend decided to end session; then reconnects fail due to billing/auth returning 402. That would produce partial output for clients expecting the final event.

Customer Rep (Acme): The customers say tokens are short-lived (mobile SDK rotates every 15m). This stream lasts ~30s, so rotation shouldn't be in-flight, but they do rotate aggressively on background refreshes. Could rotation race with reconnect?

Matt (eng-runtime): Yes — two failure modes: 1) token validation mid-stream (we mark as revoked and close session), 2) resume requests using a new token that isn't yet accepted by billing plane because of propagation delay -> 402 or 401. If client does immediate reconnect with new token, but billing sync hasn't seen updated entitlement, reconnect will fail.

ReproBot: Automated repro attempt against customer token (sanitized) reproduced partial output twice. Captured HTTP headers showing: Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token-v2>, X-Resume-Token: rsm-45df, and the second connection returned 402 with body: {"error":"account_over_quota"}.

Matt (eng-runtime): Can you also check our metrics? I want to see per-account 402 spikes and rate of 'token_revoked' signals. @Jordan can you graph account.acme 402 rate and billing-service notifications for last 6h?

Jordan (sre): On it. Quick look: acme account had a burst of billing-service 'limit_reached' at 19:12:50 across three endpoints. 402 count jumps from 0 -> 17 in 2 minutes. Here's the console query I ran: 

```
sum(rate(http_responses_total{status="402",account="acme",path=~"/v1/streams.*"}[5m])) by (account)
```

Jordan (sre): Also saw a small spike in auth-cache-miss which could cause a short window where new tokens aren't validated by the auth plane. That's likely the propagation race.

Alyssa (support): For immediate customer help: recommend these steps: 
- Ask customers to retry with exponential backoff on reconnects (jitter + backoff to allow billing sync).
- If they can, swap to a non-rotating token for long-lived streams until we fix.
- Provide a short mitigation: server-side stream finalize: we can add a finalization event before closing when we detect billing signal (fast patch).

Matt (eng-runtime): Agreed. Long-term fix items: 
- Add atomic resume token validation that decouples auth propagation for resume flows.
- Emit explicit stream-end event when we close due to billing/auth reasons with a machine-readable code so clients can attribute (e.g., event: stream_end; reason: billing_limit).
- Improve observability: correlate trace_id -> billing-notification-id in logs.

Customer Rep (Acme): Can you share an interim test build/instrumented endpoint so I can confirm with customers? They need a visible stream_end event to avoid UI hang.

Matt (eng-runtime): I'll spin up an instrumented canary route: /v1/streams-beta/instrumented for ACME account only. It will: 
- emit 'event: __redwood_end__ reason=billing_limit' before closing, 
- log trace id and billing notification id.

Give me ~45m.

Jordan (sre): Action items: 
- Jordan: correlate billing notifications to 402 spike and attach timeline (in progress).
- Matt: canary endpoint + patch to emit final event (45m).
- Alyssa: send interim mitigation to customer (backoff + non-rotating token) and request reproduction window (19:10-19:20).
- ReproBot: run scheduled harness across multiple token rotation windows to assert flakiness.

Alyssa (support): I'm sending the note now and will attach the pcap and trace id. Will update ticket ACME-789 with the fix plan. :thumbsup:

Inc-Bot: Incident created INC-2026-0310-ACME-STREAM, severity=low, assignees=[Matt, Jordan, Alyssa]

Matt (eng-runtime): One more: engineers, please do not assume streaming sockets won't be closed for billing reasons. Client SDKs should show partial output and surface a clear message like 'stream ended: billing_limit' rather than spinner. We'll add the server final event to make this deterministic.

Customer Rep (Acme): Thanks team — customers will appreciate the explicit end event. I'll keep the thread updated after I test the beta endpoint.

(End of thread)
